statement: Fix τ = σ = 1 − 2−50 , β = 1 2 , C1 = 20. Let c, ϵ, λ, λ′ be fixed positive rational numbers satisfying max{τ, σ} < λ < 1, τ(1 + c/β) < λ, max{λ, σ + β(1 − σ)} < λ′ < 1, ϵC1 < 1. Fix positive constants ad ≤ bd and ar ≤ br, and fix positive constants CM , Cdesc, Cw with Cw > 1. For these fixed choices there are a cutoff p0, one fixed finite-alphabet multitape procedure, and an implicit time constant with the following guarantee. The cutoff and time constant may depend on the fixed rational parameters and these constants. For every choice of positive integers p, d, r with p ≥ p0 and adpϵ ≤ d ≤ bdpϵ , 2arp/d ≤ r ≤ 2brp/d , put K = ⌊dc⌋, and let 1 ≤ D ≤ d, P, S ≥ 1, and 0 ≤ ρ < K be integers. Let w ≥ 1 be an integer component width. The input supplies on a descriptor tape the self-delimiting header E = Γ(p)Γ(d)Γ(r)Γ(D)Γ(P)Γ(S)Γ(K)Γ(ρ + 1)Γ(w), 36 using the integer code from (1). Assume that this header is valid with the stated values and that the accompanying array is in lexicographic order on the complete address set [P] × [2K ]D × [S], M = PS 2KD , with the following record format. For every address x ∈ [P] × [2K]D × [S], write its record as z(x) = r−1 X j=0 zx,jyj , stored in coefficient order. For every x and 0 ≤ j < r, assume |zx,j| ≤ 1 and ℜzx,j, ℑzx,j ∈ 2−pZ. Each component is 2−p times a signed w-bit two’s-complement integer, written most significant bit first; the real component precedes the imaginary component. Require the pointwise bounds log2(2M) ≤ CM p, |E| ≤ Cdescp, p + 2 ≤ w ≤ Cwp, where |E| is the header’s bit length. The condition w ≥ p + 2 allows every permitted disk-grid component, including −1 and 1. The logical bit volume is V = 2Mrw = Θ(Mrp). On each of the D consecutive K-bit address chunks, select bit ρ, numbered from the least significant bit, and let H be the tensor product of H0 = 1 2 1 1 1 −1 ! on those selected bits. It acts coefficientwise and fixes every unselected address bit and both spectator fields. Let Qp truncate the real and imaginary parts of every coefficient toward zero to 2−pZ. The procedure returns Qp(Hz) in the same array, coefficient order, and component format in O(V dλ′ ) time, uniformly over all these choices of p, d, r, D, P, S, ρ, w and z. Every returned coefficient belongs to the complex unit disk, and, in the maximum coefficient norm, ∥Qp(Hz) − Hz∥∞ < √ 2 2−p . The procedure evaluates the entire layer exactly before this final truncation. Put C0 = 128m sc + 64(Wc + m + 1)32 , where m, Wc, sc are the fixed constants of Proposition 8. The procedure uses at most p + ⌈C0dC1 ⌉ fractional bits and ⌈C0dC1 ⌉ + 3 integer and sign bits per real component internally; these widths are O(p). The time includes address changes, deterministic repair, row padding and its removal, and fixed-tape workspace cleanup. Its tape count is fixed, and its time constant is independent of the allowed array lengths and coefficient values.
